Tools\u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eSpring AI Playground is a cross-platform desktop app for building, testing, validating, and executing MCP tools in a controlled local environment. It helps you create reusable MCP tools once and use them across macOS, Windows, and Linux through a self-contained runtime. Unlike platforms that focus primarily on generating agents or authoring tools, Spring AI Playground focuses on making the tools it manages inside the app safer and easier to inspect before reuse.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cblockquote\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eNo pass, no run.\u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003c/blockquote\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eEvery tool you build earns a \u003cstrong\u003eLocal Pass\u003c/strong\u003e — a local test-run with your sample arguments. Only passing tools are added live to the built-in MCP server and become callable from Agentic Chat. A tool that has not passed is never exposed to an agent.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cblockquote\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eSecurity scope.\u003c/strong\u003e The in-process sandbox is defense-in-depth for the local build-and-vet loop. It is not adversarial-grade isolation and not a gateway. To run tool code you do not trust, nest it in container or microVM isolation. See \u003ca href=\"https://spring-ai-community.github.io/spring-ai-playground/safety-architecture/#isolation-tiers\" rel=\"nofollow\"\u003eIsolation tiers\u003c/a\u003e.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003c/blockquote\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eSafe execution does not end at publication. Every chat, tool call, vector lookup, and MCP invocation that runs in the app lands in the built-in \u003cstrong\u003eObservability dashboards\u003c/strong\u003e spanning Overview, Tokens \u0026amp; Cost, AI Models, Tool Studio, MCP Servers, MCP Inspector, Vector Database, Agentic Chat, Safety, Host, Ollama, Web Application, Logs, and Traces, backed by a ring buffer with dated disk persistence. Drill from a row into the trace timeline and raw spans, jump to the conversation thread, and deep-link back into Agentic Chat — so the tools you let an agent call are also the tools you can see in detail after the fact.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eIn Tool Studio, new or updated built-in tools are test-run before they are published to the built-in MCP server. You do not need to know Java, Spring, or JVM internals to use it. If you can install a desktop app and write a small JavaScript function, you can build tools here and connect them to hosts and clients such as Claude Desktop, Claude Code, Cursor, IDEs, and other MCP-compatible environments.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eShips with a \u003cstrong\u003ebundled catalog of default tools\u003c/strong\u003e — web fetch, datetime, math, security, encoding, crypto, filesystem, GitHub, Wikipedia, weather, finance, geo, and a Korean-domain bundle (Upbit, Bithumb, Naver, Kakao, KMA, KOFIC, KRX, data.go.kr keychain) — searchable and filterable in the \u003ca href=\"/spring-ai-community/spring-ai-playground/blob/main/docs/features/default-tools/index.md#browse-all-tools\"\u003eDefault Tools directory\u003c/a\u003e.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003ePlus a \u003cstrong\u003epreset catalog of external MCP servers\u003c/strong\u003e — Gmail, Notion, Slack, GitHub, Linear, Atlassian, Tavily, Firecrawl, Microsoft-Teams, Sentry, and more — grouped by category with \u003ccode\u003e${ENV_VAR}\u003c/code\u003e placeholders so disabled servers can't be activated without setup. Privacy \u0026amp; Security\u003c/strong\u003e and click \u003cstrong\u003eOpen Anyway\u003c/strong\u003e.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003eAfter copying the app into \u003cstrong\u003eApplications\u003c/strong\u003e, macOS may block the first app launch again. If that happens, open the app once, then return to \u003cstrong\u003eSystem Settings \u0026gt; Privacy \u0026amp; Security\u003c/strong\u003e and click \u003cstrong\u003eOpen Anyway\u003c/strong\u003e.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003c/ul\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eIf the app still doesn’t open because it remains quarantined, and you trust the app, one practical workaround is:\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cdiv class=\"snippet-clipboard-content notranslate position-relative overflow-auto\" data-snippet-clipboard-copy-content=\"xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine \u0026quot;/Applications/Spring AI Playground.app\u0026quot;\"\u003e\u003cpre class=\"notranslate\"\u003e\u003ccode\u003exattr -dr com.apple.quarantine \"/Applications/Spring AI Playground.app\"\n\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/pre\u003e\u003c/div\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eWindows\u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eThe most common warning appears when you run the downloaded installer (\u003ccode\u003e.exe\u003c/code\u003e).\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eIf Microsoft Defender SmartScreen shows a warning such as “Windows protected your PC” or says the app is unrecognized:\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cul dir=\"auto\"\u003e\n\u003cli\u003eClick \u003cstrong\u003eMore info\u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003eThen click \u003cstrong\u003eRun anyway\u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003c/ul\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eLinux\u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eSeparate Gatekeeper- or SmartScreen-style reputation warnings are uncommon. When installing the \u003ccode\u003e.deb\u003c/code\u003e or \u003ccode\u003e.rpm\u003c/code\u003e package, you usually only need to complete the normal package-install confirmation steps.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eFor more detailed platform guidance, see the \u003ca href=\"https://spring-ai-community.github.io/spring-ai-playground/getting-started/\" rel=\"nofollow\"\u003eGetting Started guide\u003c/a\u003e.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003c/blockquote\u003e\n\u003cdiv class=\"markdown-heading\" dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003ch3 tabindex=\"-1\" class=\"heading-element\" dir=\"auto\"\u003eVerify Your Download\u003c/h3\u003e\u003ca id=\"user-content-verify-your-download\" class=\"anchor\" aria-label=\"Permalink: Verify Your Download\" href=\"#verify-your-download\"\u003e\u003csvg data-component=\"Octicon\" class=\"octicon octicon-link\" viewBox=\"0 0 16 16\" version=\"1.1\" width=\"16\" height=\"16\" aria-hidden=\"true\"\u003e\u003cpath d=\"m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z\"\u003e\u003c/path\u003e\u003c/svg\u003e\u003c/a\u003e\u003c/div\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eEvery release ships with a matching \u003ccode\u003e.sha256\u003c/code\u003e checksum file and a Sigstore SLSA build provenance attestation. The same Spring Boot fat JAR drives every channel; switching to a stdio MCP transport is opt-in via the \u003ccode\u003emcp-stdio\u003c/code\u003e Spring profile.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eFor the \u003cstrong\u003eapp/web experience\u003c/strong\u003e (default — \u003ccode\u003estreamable-http\u003c/code\u003e MCP server on port 8282, Vaadin UI front and center):\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cul dir=\"auto\"\u003e\n\u003cli\u003eDocker — \u003ccode\u003edocker run -p 8282:8282 -v spring-ai-playground:/root ghcr.io/spring-ai-community/spring-ai-playground\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003eLocal source run — \u003ccode\u003e./mvnw -Pproduction spring-boot:run\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003c/ul\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eFor the \u003cstrong\u003estdio MCP server\u003c/strong\u003e (drop-in for Claude Desktop, Claude Code, IDEs, and any other MCP-compatible client) — set \u003ccode\u003eSPRING_PROFILES_INCLUDE=mcp-stdio\u003c/code\u003e to layer the stdio transport on top of the default profile (so model config like Ollama / OpenAI is preserved):\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cul dir=\"auto\"\u003e\n\u003cli\u003eDocker — \u003ccode\u003edocker run -i --rm -e SPRING_PROFILES_INCLUDE=mcp-stdio -v spring-ai-playground:/root ghcr.io/spring-ai-community/spring-ai-playground\u003c/code\u003e. Add \u003ccode\u003e-p 8282:8282\u003c/code\u003e if you also want browser access to the Vaadin Inspector alongside the stdio channel.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003eRaw fat JAR — download \u003ccode\u003espring-ai-playground-*.jar\u003c/code\u003e from \u003ca href=\"https://github.com/spring-ai-community/spring-ai-playground/releases\"\u003eReleases\u003c/a\u003e (or \u003ccode\u003e./mvnw -Pproduction package\u003c/code\u003e) and run \u003ccode\u003eSPRING_PROFILES_INCLUDE=mcp-stdio java -jar spring-ai-playground-*.jar\u003c/code\u003e. No Docker required, ideal for Java/Spring developers and CI integrations.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003c/ul\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eFull setup details for both modes live in \u003ca dir=\"auto\"\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eBuilt-In MCP Server\u003c/strong\u003e: Publish tools directly from the app and expose them immediately through the built-in MCP server instead of wiring ad-hoc local scripts by hand.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eExternal MCP Catalog\u003c/strong\u003e: a preset catalog of external MCP server connections (Gmail, Notion, Slack, GitHub, Linear, Atlassian, Tavily, Microsoft-Teams, Sentry, and more) grouped by category with \u003ccode\u003e${ENV_VAR}\u003c/code\u003e placeholders so disabled servers can't be activated without setup. One-click activation from the sidebar once the required env vars exist. Browse the full list in the \u003ca href=\"/spring-ai-community/spring-ai-playground/blob/main/docs/features/default-mcp-catalog/index.md\"\u003eDefault MCP Catalog\u003c/a\u003e.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eMCP Server Proxy\u003c/strong\u003e: Select tools from any connected external MCP server and re-expose them on the built-in \u003ccode\u003e/mcp\u003c/code\u003e endpoint — compose multiple servers into one surface callable from Agentic Chat, the Inspector, and external MCP clients, each gated by per-tool human-in-the-loop.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eNo Pass, No Run Workflow\u003c/strong\u003e: A new tool starts as a \u003cstrong\u003eDraft\u003c/strong\u003e — invisible to the MCP server and to chat. It only crosses the exposure gate after a Local Pass (a successful test run with its declared sample inputs), making validation part of the default product flow instead of an optional afterthought.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eBuilt-in MCP Server Native Tools\u003c/strong\u003e: The launcher's Default MCP Tools card and Tool Studio's Built-in MCP Server Native Tools drawer both edit the same \u003ccode\u003edefault-tools-preference.json\u003c/code\u003e — pick a preset (\u003ccode\u003eStarter 5\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003eDev Essentials\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003eKorea Toolkit\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003eFile Toolkit\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003eEverything\u003c/code\u003e) plus optional per-tool include / exclude rules to decide exactly which subset of the bundled tools the built-in MCP server exposes.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eExecutable Tool Validation\u003c/strong\u003e: Test tools with real inputs, outputs, and runtime constraints before you reuse them from other MCP-compatible hosts and clients.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eDefense-in-depth Sandbox + Risk Level\u003c/strong\u003e: Every tool runs through a deny-first class allowlist, SSRF-guarded \u003ccode\u003efetch\u003c/code\u003e, rooted \u003ccode\u003esafety.fs\u003c/code\u003e, statement and wall-clock limits, with a visible per-tool \u003cstrong\u003eRisk Level (L0–L5)\u003c/strong\u003e computed from the declared capabilities — surface every tool's blast radius before you publish it.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eHuman-in-the-Loop Approval\u003c/strong\u003e: Sensitive tool calls pause for explicit approval — both Agentic Chat and the built-in MCP server gate per-tool execution behind a human confirmation, so an agent never runs a risky tool without your sign-off.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eSecure Secret Management\u003c/strong\u003e: API keys and sensitive configuration stay out of YAML and live in the desktop app's secret storage or \u003ccode\u003e${ENV_VAR}\u003c/code\u003e placeholders that resolve at tool / MCP load time. \u003cstrong\u003eSecretMasking\u003c/strong\u003e redacts any resolved value (≥ 4 characters) from error logs and console output. When OS-backed secure storage is unavailable, the app clearly warns before falling back to plain-text local storage.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eTool-to-Agent Workflow\u003c/strong\u003e: Create tools in Tool Studio, inspect them through MCP, and use them in Agentic Chat in one continuous workflow.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eProvider Agnostic\u003c/strong\u003e: Switch between Ollama, OpenAI, and other OpenAI-compatible APIs without changing the overall workflow.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eOS-Independent Tool Runtime\u003c/strong\u003e: Tools are authored once as JavaScript and run through the same bundled runtime, so the same tool definition works consistently across macOS, Windows, and Linux.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eSingle-Agent Execution\u003c/strong\u003e: Use validated built-in tools together with grounded context (RAG) in Agentic Chat to handle focused, practical workflows without needing a larger orchestration layer. Agentic Chat can also call tools exposed by MCP servers that you explicitly connect and trust.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eAgentic Chat Workbench\u003c/strong\u003e: A Prompt Library of ready-to-use presets and \u003ccode\u003e{{variable}}\u003c/code\u003e templates, per-turn reasoning effort (Off/Low/Medium/High), a configurable per-chat memory window, dynamic tool discovery, image attachments as native multimodal input for vision models, review-then-act action cards (email, calendar, map), clickable file paths, on-device voice input, and rich rendering of syntax-highlighted code, KaTeX math, and Mermaid diagrams. See \u003ca href=\"/spring-ai-community/spring-ai-playground/blob/main/docs/features/agentic-chat/index.md\"\u003eAgentic Chat\u003c/a\u003e.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eObservability Dashboards\u003c/strong\u003e: Built-in dashboards spanning Overview, Tokens \u0026amp; Cost, AI Models, Tool Studio, MCP Servers, MCP Inspector, Vector Database, Agentic Chat, Safety, Host, Ollama, Web Application, Logs, and Traces, backed by an in-memory ring buffer with dated disk persistence. Drill from a row into the trace timeline and raw spans, jump to the full conversation thread, and deep-link straight back into Agentic Chat.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003c/ul\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eThe intended workflow is practical and composable:\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cul dir=\"auto\"\u003e\n\u003cli\u003ecreate or adapt tools in Tool Studio (drafts stay private until they pass)\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003etest them before publishing — the Local Pass is what opens the MCP exposure gate\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003ecurate which bundled defaults the MCP server exposes alongside your own tools\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003einspect everything live through MCP Inspector\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003eindex knowledge in Vector Database\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003ecombine tools and documents in Agentic Chat\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003c/ul\u003e\n\u003cdiv class=\"markdown-heading\" dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003ch2 tabindex=\"-1\" AI; as Spring AI and the ecosystem moved toward agents and MCP, it grew into a safe local execution layer for the tools agents call.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eIt also doubles as a working reference implementation of the Spring AI framework — every surface in the app maps to a real Spring AI API, so you can use this repo as an end-to-end example of how those pieces fit together.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cul dir=\"auto\"\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eChatClient + advisor pipeline\u003c/strong\u003e drives Agentic Chat — message memory, the \u003ccode\u003eRetrievalAugmentationAdvisor\u003c/code\u003e for RAG, and the Tool Calling pipeline are composed through \u003ccode\u003eChatClient.builder()\u003c/code\u003e and a custom \u003ccode\u003eSpringAiPlaygroundRagAdvisor\u003c/code\u003e.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eMCP client and server starters together\u003c/strong\u003e — \u003ccode\u003espring-ai-starter-mcp-client\u003c/code\u003e connects to the external MCP servers in the preset catalog and to the built-in MCP server in the same JVM, while \u003ccode\u003espring-ai-starter-mcp-server-webmvc\u003c/code\u003e publishes every Local-Pass tool you author through the \u003ccode\u003espring-ai-playground-tool-mcp\u003c/code\u003e connection on \u003ccode\u003e/mcp\u003c/code\u003e.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eTool Calling Manager + custom \u003ccode\u003eToolCallback\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/strong\u003e — Tool Studio tools and external MCP tools both run through a single \u003ccode\u003eAgentLoopManager\u003c/code\u003e (the app's \u003ccode\u003eToolCallingManager\u003c/code\u003e, adding per-turn round bounds and the human-in-the-loop gate), with \u003ccode\u003eLoggingMcpToolCallback\u003c/code\u003e adding correlation ids and secret masking around every call.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eVector store + ETL pipeline\u003c/strong\u003e — \u003ccode\u003eSimpleVectorStore\u003c/code\u003e plus the Spring AI Tika document reader power Vector Database, exposed through the same reader / chunker / pre-retrieval / retrieval / post-retrieval stages the framework ships.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eMicrometer Observation API\u003c/strong\u003e — \u003ccode\u003eObservationRegistry\u003c/code\u003e is wired into \u003ccode\u003eToolCallingManager\u003c/code\u003e and \u003ccode\u003eSimpleVectorStore\u003c/code\u003e, so spans emitted by Spring AI's semantic conventions (\u003ccode\u003egen_ai.client.operation\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003espring.ai.chat.client\u003c/code\u003e) flow straight into the in-app Observability dashboards alongside chat-client spans.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003c/ul\u003e\n\u003cp <p dir="auto"><strong>Safe Local Execution Layer for AI Agent Tools</strong></p>
<p dir="auto">Spring AI Playground is a cross-platform desktop app for building, testing, validating, and executing MCP tools in a controlled local environment. It helps you create reusable MCP tools once and use them across macOS, Windows, and Linux through a self-contained runtime. Unlike platforms that focus primarily on generating agents or authoring tools, Spring AI Playground focuses on making the tools it manages inside the app safer and easier to inspect before reuse.</p>
<blockquote>
<p dir="auto"><strong>No pass, no run.</strong></p>
</blockquote>
<p dir="auto">Every tool you build earns a <strong>Local Pass</strong> — a local test-run with your sample arguments. Only passing tools are added live to the built-in MCP server and become callable from Agentic Chat. A tool that has not passed is never exposed to an agent.</p>
<blockquote>
<p dir="auto"><strong>Security scope.</strong> The in-process sandbox is defense-in-depth for the local build-and-vet loop. It is not adversarial-grade isolation and not a gateway. To run tool code you do not trust, nest it in container or microVM isolation. See <a href="https://spring-ai-community.github.io/spring-ai-playground/safety-architecture/#isolation-tiers" rel="nofollow">Isolation tiers</a>.</p>
</blockquote>
<p dir="auto">Safe execution does not end at publication. Every chat, tool call, vector lookup, and MCP invocation that runs in the app lands in the built-in <strong>Observability dashboards</strong> spanning Overview, Tokens & Cost, AI Models, Tool Studio, MCP Servers, MCP Inspector, Vector Database, Agentic Chat, Safety, Host, Ollama, Web Application, Logs, and Traces, backed by a ring buffer with dated disk persistence. Drill from a row into the trace timeline and raw spans, jump to the conversation thread, and deep-link back into Agentic Chat — so the tools you let an agent call are also the tools you can see in detail after the fact.</p>
<p dir="auto">In Tool Studio, new or updated built-in tools are test-run before they are published to the built-in MCP server. You do not need to know Java, Spring, or JVM internals to use it. If you can install a desktop app and write a small JavaScript function, you can build tools here and connect them to hosts and clients such as Claude Desktop, Claude Code, Cursor, IDEs, and other MCP-compatible environments.</p>
<p dir="auto">Ships with a <strong>bundled catalog of default tools</strong> — web fetch, datetime, math, security, encoding, crypto, filesystem, GitHub, Wikipedia, weather, finance, geo, and a Korean-domain bundle (Upbit, Bithumb, Naver, Kakao, KMA, KOFIC, KRX, data.go.kr keychain) — searchable and filterable in the <a href="/spring-ai-community/spring-ai-playground/blob/main/docs/features/default-tools/index.md#browse-all-tools">Default Tools directory</a>.</p>
<p dir="auto">Plus a <strong>preset catalog of external MCP servers</strong> — Gmail, Notion, Slack, GitHub, Linear, Atlassian, Tavily, Firecrawl, Microsoft-Teams, Sentry, and more — grouped by category with <code>${ENV_VAR}</code> placeholders so disabled servers can't be activated without setup. Browse the full list in the <a href="/spring-ai-community/spring-ai-playground/blob/main/docs/features/default-mcp-catalog/index.md">Default MCP Catalog</a>.</p>

<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h2 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">The Problem</h2><a id="user-content-the-problem" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: The Problem" href="#the-problem"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto">AI agents can generate tools quickly, but generated tools are not inherently safe to execute.</p>
<ul dir="auto">
<li>It is often unclear what actually runs at execution time</li>
<li>Failures are difficult to predict before real usage</li>
<li>Execution is not easily traceable or inspectable</li>
</ul>
<p dir="auto">Most platforms focus on creation.</p>
<p dir="auto">Very few make verification part of the default workflow for built-in tool publication, and even fewer leave a clear trail of what each tool actually did after it ran. Spring AI Playground treats both as part of safe local execution — Local Pass at the gate, Observability dashboards on the inside.</p>
<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h2 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">Who is this for?</h2><a id="user-content-who-is-this-for" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: Who is this for?" href="#who-is-this-for"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<ul dir="auto">
<li>Developers building MCP tools who want validation built into the default workflow</li>
<li>Teams running MCP tools in agent host environments (Claude Code, Cursor, IDE plugins, mixed-stack runtimes) who need a stable local execution layer instead of ad-hoc local scripts</li>
<li>Teams who need a clear, local audit trail of token cost, latency, and per-call traces for chat, tool, vector, and MCP invocations</li>
<li>Spring developers looking for a working end-to-end reference implementation of Spring AI's ChatClient, MCP client/server, RAG advisor, vector store, and Observation API</li>
<li>Users of Claude Desktop, Claude Code, Cursor, and other MCP-compatible environments</li>
</ul>
<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h2 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">Quick Start</h2><a id="user-content-quick-start" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: Quick Start" href="#quick-start"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>

<p dir="auto">Spring AI Playground is a standalone desktop app, so you can install it and start building MCP tools without setting up a Java project, Docker environment, or source build first.</p>

Install and Launch" href="#2-install-and-launch"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto">Install the app like a normal desktop application, then launch <strong>Spring AI Playground</strong> from your applications menu.</p>
<p dir="auto">The desktop app bundles the backend runtime together with a launcher that provides provider starter templates, YAML override editing, environment-variable based secret handling, and one-click launch.</p>
<p dir="auto">If you install the app, you can run Spring AI Playground immediately without setting up Docker or running the source manually.</p>
<blockquote>
<p dir="auto"><strong>macOS</strong></p>
<p dir="auto">Gatekeeper may block the install flow in two places:</p>
<ul dir="auto">
<li>When you open the downloaded DMG, macOS may show a warning such as “cannot be opened because the developer cannot be verified.” If you trust the release source, go to <strong>System Settings > Privacy & Security</strong> and click <strong>Open Anyway</strong>.</li>
<li>After copying the app into <strong>Applications</strong>, macOS may block the first app launch again. If that happens, open the app once, then return to <strong>System Settings > Privacy & Security</strong> and click <strong>Open Anyway</strong>.</li>
</ul>
<p dir="auto">If the app still doesn’t open because it remains quarantined, and you trust the app, one practical workaround is:</p>
<div class="snippet-clipboard-content notranslate position-relative overflow-auto" data-snippet-clipboard-copy-content="xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine "/Applications/Spring AI Playground.app""><pre class="notranslate"><code>xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine "/Applications/Spring AI Playground.app"
</code></pre></div>
<p dir="auto"><strong>Windows</strong></p>
<p dir="auto">The most common warning appears when you run the downloaded installer (<code>.exe</code>).</p>
<p dir="auto">If Microsoft Defender SmartScreen shows a warning such as “Windows protected your PC” or says the app is unrecognized:</p>
<ul dir="auto">
<li>Click <strong>More info</strong></li>
<li>Then click <strong>Run anyway</strong></li>
</ul>
<p dir="auto"><strong>Linux</strong></p>

<p dir="auto">Alternative runtimes are still supported. The same Spring Boot fat JAR drives every channel; switching to a stdio MCP transport is opt-in via the <code>mcp-stdio</code> Spring profile.</p>
<p dir="auto">For the <strong>app/web experience</strong> (default — <code>streamable-http</code> MCP server on port 8282, Vaadin UI front and center):</p>
<ul dir="auto">
<li>Docker — <code>docker run -p 8282:8282 -v spring-ai-playground:/root ghcr.io/spring-ai-community/spring-ai-playground</code></li>
<li>Local source run — <code>./mvnw -Pproduction spring-boot:run</code></li>
</ul>
<p dir="auto">For the <strong>stdio MCP server</strong> (drop-in for Claude Desktop, Claude Code, IDEs, and any other MCP-compatible client) — set <code>SPRING_PROFILES_INCLUDE=mcp-stdio</code> to layer the stdio transport on top of the default profile (so model config like Ollama / OpenAI is preserved):</p>
<ul dir="auto">
<li>Docker — <code>docker run -i --rm -e SPRING_PROFILES_INCLUDE=mcp-stdio -v spring-ai-playground:/root ghcr.io/spring-ai-community/spring-ai-playground</code>. Add <code>-p 8282:8282</code> if you also want browser access to the Vaadin Inspector alongside the stdio channel.</li>
<li>Raw fat JAR — download <code>spring-ai-playground-*.jar</code> from <a href="https://github.com/spring-ai-community/spring-ai-playground/releases">Releases</a> (or <code>./mvnw -Pproduction package</code>) and run <code>SPRING_PROFILES_INCLUDE=mcp-stdio java -jar spring-ai-playground-*.jar</code>. No Docker required, ideal for Java/Spring developers and CI integrations.</li>
</ul>
<p dir="auto">Full setup details for both modes live in <a href="https://spring-ai-community.github.io/spring-ai-playground/getting-started/alternative-runtimes/" rel="nofollow">Getting Started: Alternative Runtimes</a>.</p>
<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h2 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">Why Spring AI Playground?</h2><a id="user-content-why-spring-ai-playground" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: Why Spring AI Playground?" href="#why-spring-ai-playground"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<ul dir="auto">
<li><strong>Built-In MCP Server</strong>: Publish tools directly from the app and expose them immediately through the built-in MCP server instead of wiring ad-hoc local scripts by hand.</li>
<li><strong>External MCP Catalog</strong>: a preset catalog of external MCP server connections (Gmail, Notion, Slack, GitHub, Linear, Atlassian, Tavily, Microsoft-Teams, Sentry, and more) grouped by category with <code>${ENV_VAR}</code> placeholders so disabled servers can't be activated without setup. One-click activation from the sidebar once the required env vars exist. Browse the full list in the <a href="/spring-ai-community/spring-ai-playground/blob/main/docs/features/default-mcp-catalog/index.md">Default MCP Catalog</a>.</li>
<li><strong>MCP Server Proxy</strong>: Select tools from any connected external MCP server and re-expose them on the built-in <code>/mcp</code> endpoint — compose multiple servers into one surface callable from Agentic Chat, the Inspector, and external MCP clients, each gated by per-tool human-in-the-loop.</li>
<li><strong>No Pass, No Run Workflow</strong>: A new tool starts as a <strong>Draft</strong> — invisible to the MCP server and to chat. It only crosses the exposure gate after a Local Pass (a successful test run with its declared sample inputs), making validation part of the default product flow instead of an optional afterthought.</li>
<li><strong>Built-in MCP Server Native Tools</strong>: The launcher's Default MCP Tools card and Tool Studio's Built-in MCP Server Native Tools drawer both edit the same <code>default-tools-preference.json</code> — pick a preset (<code>Starter 5</code>, <code>Dev Essentials</code>, <code>Korea Toolkit</code>, <code>File Toolkit</code>, <code>Everything</code>) plus optional per-tool include / exclude rules to decide exactly which subset of the bundled tools the built-in MCP server exposes.</li>
<li><strong>Executable Tool Validation</strong>: Test tools with real inputs, outputs, and runtime constraints before you reuse them from other MCP-compatible hosts and clients.</li>
<li><strong>Defense-in-depth Sandbox + Risk Level</strong>: Every tool runs through a deny-first class allowlist, SSRF-guarded <code>fetch</code>, rooted <code>safety.fs</code>, statement and wall-clock limits, with a visible per-tool <strong>Risk Level (L0–L5)</strong> computed from the declared capabilities — surface every tool's blast radius before you publish it.</li>
<li><strong>Human-in-the-Loop Approval</strong>: Sensitive tool calls pause for explicit approval — both Agentic Chat and the built-in MCP server gate per-tool execution behind a human confirmation, so an agent never runs a risky tool without your sign-off.</li>
<li><strong>Secure Secret Management</strong>: API keys and sensitive configuration stay out of YAML and live in the desktop app's secret storage or <code>${ENV_VAR}</code> placeholders that resolve at tool / MCP load time. <strong>SecretMasking</strong> redacts any resolved value (≥ 4 characters) from error logs and console output. When OS-backed secure storage is unavailable, the app clearly warns before falling back to plain-text local storage.</li>
<li><strong>Tool-to-Agent Workflow</strong>: Create tools in Tool Studio, inspect them through MCP, and use them in Agentic Chat in one continuous workflow.</li>
<li><strong>Provider Agnostic</strong>: Switch between Ollama, OpenAI, and other OpenAI-compatible APIs without changing the overall workflow.</li>
<li><strong>OS-Independent Tool Runtime</strong>: Tools are authored once as JavaScript and run through the same bundled runtime, so the same tool definition works consistently across macOS, Windows, and Linux.</li>
<li><strong>Single-Agent Execution</strong>: Use validated built-in tools together with grounded context (RAG) in Agentic Chat to handle focused, practical workflows without needing a larger orchestration layer. Agentic Chat can also call tools exposed by MCP servers that you explicitly connect and trust.</li>
<li><strong>Agentic Chat Workbench</strong>: A Prompt Library of ready-to-use presets and <code>{{variable}}</code> templates, per-turn reasoning effort (Off/Low/Medium/High), a configurable per-chat memory window, dynamic tool discovery, image attachments as native multimodal input for vision models, review-then-act action cards (email, calendar, map), clickable file paths, on-device voice input, and rich rendering of syntax-highlighted code, KaTeX math, and Mermaid diagrams. See <a href="/spring-ai-community/spring-ai-playground/blob/main/docs/features/agentic-chat/index.md">Agentic Chat</a>.</li>
<li><strong>Observability Dashboards</strong>: Built-in dashboards spanning Overview, Tokens & Cost, AI Models, Tool Studio, MCP Servers, MCP Inspector, Vector Database, Agentic Chat, Safety, Host, Ollama, Web Application, Logs, and Traces, backed by an in-memory ring buffer with dated disk persistence. Drill from a row into the trace timeline and raw spans, jump to the full conversation thread, and deep-link straight back into Agentic Chat.</li>
</ul>
<p dir="auto">The intended workflow is practical and composable:</p>
<ul dir="auto">
<li>create or adapt tools in Tool Studio (drafts stay private until they pass)</li>
<li>test them before publishing — the Local Pass is what opens the MCP exposure gate</li>
<li>curate which bundled defaults the MCP server exposes alongside your own tools</li>
<li>inspect everything live through MCP Inspector</li>
<li>index knowledge in Vector Database</li>
<li>combine tools and documents in Agentic Chat</li>
</ul>
<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h2 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">Why Not Just Use Agent Builders?</h2><a id="user-content-why-not-just-use-agent-builders" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: Why Not Just Use Agent Builders?" href="#why-not-just-use-agent-builders"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto">Agent builders focus on generating tools and composing workflows.</p>
<p dir="auto">Spring AI Playground focuses on validating tools and controlling execution.</p>
<p dir="auto">It complements agent builders by providing a reliable execution layer.</p>
<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h2 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">Built on Spring AI</h2><a id="user-content-built-on-spring-ai" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: Built on Spring AI" href="#built-on-spring-ai"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto">Spring AI Playground started as a way to explore Spring AI; as Spring AI and the ecosystem moved toward agents and MCP, it grew into a safe local execution layer for the tools agents call.</p>
<p dir="auto">It also doubles as a working reference implementation of the Spring AI framework — every surface in the app maps to a real Spring AI API, so you can use this repo as an end-to-end example of how those pieces fit together.</p>
<ul dir="auto">
<li><strong>ChatClient + advisor pipeline</strong> drives Agentic Chat — message memory, the <code>RetrievalAugmentationAdvisor</code> for RAG, and the Tool Calling pipeline are composed through <code>ChatClient.builder()</code> and a custom <code>SpringAiPlaygroundRagAdvisor</code>.</li>
<li><strong>MCP client and server starters together</strong> — <code>spring-ai-starter-mcp-client</code> connects to the external MCP servers in the preset catalog and to the built-in MCP server in the same JVM, while <code>spring-ai-starter-mcp-server-webmvc</code> publishes every Local-Pass tool you author through the <code>spring-ai-playground-tool-mcp</code> connection on <code>/mcp</code>.</li>
<li><strong>Tool Calling Manager + custom <code>ToolCallback</code></strong> — Tool Studio tools and external MCP tools both run through a single <code>AgentLoopManager</code> (the app's <code>ToolCallingManager</code>, adding per-turn round bounds and the human-in-the-loop gate), with <code>LoggingMcpToolCallback</code> adding correlation ids and secret masking around every call.</li>
<li><strong>Vector store + ETL pipeline</strong> — <code>SimpleVectorStore</code> plus the Spring AI Tika document reader power Vector Database, exposed through the same reader / chunker / pre-retrieval / retrieval / post-retrieval stages the framework ships.</li>
<li><strong>Micrometer Observation API</strong> — <code>ObservationRegistry</code> is wired into <code>ToolCallingManager</code> and <code>SimpleVectorStore</code>, so spans emitted by Spring AI's semantic conventions (<code>gen_ai.client.operation</code>, <code>spring.ai.chat.client</code>) flow straight into the in-app Observability dashboards alongside chat-client spans.</li>
</ul>
<p dir="auto">The version tracks the latest Spring AI release; use it as a reference when integrating these same features into your own Spring Boot app.</p>
<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h2 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">Project Scope & Positioning</h2><a id="user-content-project-scope--positioning" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: Project Scope & Positioning" href="#project-scope--positioning"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto">Spring AI Playground is a <strong>tool-first environment</strong> for building, testing, validating, and operationalizing MCP tools in a practical workflow.</p>
<p dir="auto">It is best understood as a <strong>safe local execution layer for AI agent tools</strong>.</p>
<blockquote>
<p dir="auto"><strong>Note:</strong> This project is intentionally focused in its current stage.<br>
The goal is to make MCP tool building, validation, inspection, and runtime exposure simple and reliable, so the tools you create here can be reused from MCP-compatible hosts and clients such as Claude Code, Claude Desktop, IDEs, and other agent environments.</p>
</blockquote>
<p dir="auto">Current focus:</p>
<ul dir="auto">
<li>providing a UI-driven environment for building, testing, and validating MCP tools in a practical workflow</li>
<li>making test-before-publish the default path for built-in local tool exposure</li>
<li>testing tool execution flows, environment-backed tool configuration, and RAG integration in one place</li>
<li>making tools easier to inspect, easier to test, and easier to operationalize before they are reused elsewhere</li>
<li>supporting practical single-agent workflows through Agentic Chat with tools and grounded context. See <a href="https://spring-ai-community.github.io/spring-ai-playground/features/agentic-chat/#agentic-chat-architecture-overview" rel="nofollow">Agentic Chat Architecture Overview</a>.</li>
<li>promoting validated built-in tools into reusable MCP-hosted runtimes that can be shared across multiple MCP-compatible hosts and clients</li>
</ul>
<p dir="auto">It is not trying to replace the tools where agents actually run. It is designed to give you a clearer path from local tool prototype to inspectable, reusable MCP server.</p>

<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h3 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">Reporting Issues</h3><a id="user-content-reporting-issues" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: Reporting Issues" href="#reporting-issues"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto">Pick the right channel:</p>
<ul dir="auto">
<li><strong>Bug Report</strong> issue template — for reproducible app failures</li>
<li><strong>Documentation Issue</strong> template — for docs errors you can't fix via PR</li>
<li>documentation PR — for targeted fixes in <code>docs/</code> (typos, errors, broken links); open a Discussion first for README changes or new sections</li>
<li><strong>GitHub Discussions</strong> — Q&A for questions, Show and tell for examples; not Issues</li>
<li>read the project scope above before requesting broader changes</li>
</ul>
<p dir="auto">We triage issues regularly, and issues outside the current scope may be closed with guidance.</p>
<p dir="auto">If you have a contribution that fits the current scope (bug report, doc fix, usage example), submit a PR or a targeted issue. For anything else, please open a Discussion first — but be aware we may not act on it given current capacity.</p>
<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h2 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">Anonymous Usage Telemetry</h2><a id="user-content-anonymous-usage-telemetry" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: Anonymous Usage Telemetry" href="#anonymous-usage-telemetry"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto">The official build sends anonymous usage data (page views, feature-usage events such as
which model, preset, or tool kind is used, device/browser info) to the maintainer's
Google Tag Manager / Google Analytics account so the most-used features can be
prioritized. It is content-free: no prompts, documents, file names, URLs, or API keys,
and names of things you create yourself (tools, presets, custom MCP servers) are masked.
The complete event table is in the
<a href="https://spring-ai-community.github.io/spring-ai-playground/getting-started/configuration/#telemetry-events" rel="nofollow">Configuration reference</a>,
and every sender is auditable in code (search for <code>UsageEventTracker</code>). IPs are
anonymized by Google. Development-mode runs never send telemetry. The same opt-out
switch applies to both the web app and every desktop launcher window (splash,
server-splash, config editor, Ollama manager):</p>
<ul dir="auto">
<li><strong>Server / Docker / <code>mvn</code></strong>: <code>SPRING_AI_PLAYGROUND_TELEMETRY_ENABLED=false</code></li>
<li><strong>Desktop launcher</strong>: set <code>SPRING_AI_PLAYGROUND_TELEMETRY_ENABLED=false</code> before launching
the app (the launcher forwards this env var to every window and to the bundled Spring
process)</li>
<li><strong>From source / IDE</strong>: pass <code>-Dspring.ai.playground.telemetry.enabled=false</code> as a JVM arg</li>
</ul>
<p dir="auto">If you self-host this project for EU users, adding cookie consent on top is the
operator's responsibility under GDPR.</p>
